Ansell-OK opened issue #98: Intermittent Bolt result decoding failure with neo4j-driver
## Summary

HydraDB intermittently causes the Neo4j JavaScript driver to throw RangeError [ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE] while reading a normal Bolt query result. Retrying the identical query often succeeds.

## Environment

- HydraDB repository commit: 6a2fbb1
- Node.js: 22.19.0
- 
eo4j-driver: 5.28.2
- Client: JavaScript/TypeScript client using the Bolt endpoint

## Observed error

`	ext
RangeError [ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE]: The value of offset is out of range. It must be >= 0 and <= 3. Received 4
    at captureStacktrace (.../neo4j-driver-core/lib/result.js:624:17)
    at new Result (.../neo4j-driver-core/lib/result.js:112:23)
    at Session._run (.../neo4j-driver-core/lib/session.js:224:16)
    at Session.run (.../neo4j-driver-core/lib/session.js:188:27)
`

The failure is raised while constructing a 
eo4j-driver Result, before application rows are returned. In our client it occurred during ordinary MERGE/MATCH writes and cleanup queries while extracting a five-file JavaScript repository into HydraDB. The same query sequence can succeed on the next attempt without changing the query or parameters.

## Impact

This makes otherwise valid graph extraction and CI checks fail nondeterministically. A cl ...

aetosdios27 commented: thanks for the detailed repro. would love to help track this down.

could you share the extractor/repository fixture and the client trace? want to reproduce locally against a fresh `graph-node` instance and capture the raw bytes on the wire when it fails, rather than guess from the encoder alone.

did a pass through `boltr`'s encode path first to rule out the obvious stuff:
- `ChunkWriter` handles the 65535-byte chunk boundary correctly, including exact multiples, terminator is always appended
- PackStream `encode.rs` — every header (`STRING_8/16/32`, `LIST_*`, `DICT_*`, `BYTES_*`) derives its length from the actual payload length, nothing stale or hardcoded
- struct headers for RECORD/SUCCESS/NODE/RELATIONSHIP/PATH match their declared field counts

so this isn't a static off-by-one in the encoder as far as I can tell. given it's intermittent and tied to a specific bulk workload, my guess is it needs an actual byte-level capture to pin down rather than more code reading. happy to set up a repro harness (loop the same UNWIND/MERGE/SET shape against a local node, tcpdump the Bolt port) once I have the fixture.

Ansell-OK commented: Thanks. We tightened the reproduction and can now confirm this is not an application-level Conflict Radar error.

We reproduced the failure against a fresh HydraDB Docker node using:

- HydraDB: official `ghcr.io/hydra-db/hydradb:latest` image
- Node.js: `22.19.0`
- `neo4j-driver`: `5.28.2`
- Bolt: `bolt://127.0.0.1:17687`
- Database: `default`
- Windows 11 host

The client was a minimal direct Neo4j driver harness with the retry layer disabled. It failed on the first write, before any application rows were returned:

```text
RangeError [ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE]: The value of "offset" is out of range.
It must be >= 0 and <= 4. Received 5
```

The failing query shape was:

```cypher
UNWIND $rows AS row
MERGE (r {id: row.id})
SET r:Repo, r.name = row.name, r.path = row.path
```

Parameters were one row containing an integer `id`, repository name, and local path. The error was raised while `neo4j-driver` constructed the `Result`, not while decoding an application record.

We also ran the same retry-free workload successfully for 300 iterations. That control run produced a 645 KB loopback Bolt capture containing the handshake and query/result exchange. The failure is therefore intermittent an ...

Ansell-OK commented: We published the retry-free application trace here:

https://gist.github.com/Ansell-OK/2b25f82cea8bf94c284fa9979d0fbd62

The trace contains the exact query label, elapsed time, query text, parameter keys, and full `RangeError [ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE]` stack.

We also captured a successful 645 KB loopback Bolt control exchange from the same endpoint/workload family:

```text
hydradb-issue-98.pcapng
size: 645,700 bytes
```

GitHub gists do not accept binary uploads, so we have not put the `.pcapng` on a public file host without your preference. We can provide it through whatever artifact channel HydraDB prefers.

At this point we recommend treating the next contribution as a diagnostic/regression PR rather than a speculative encoder fix. We can submit the minimal repeated `UNWIND`/`MERGE` harness, opt-in Bolt frame logging, and assertions around response boundaries/declared field counts as a draft PR if that would be useful. Once the malformed response is identified, we can turn it into a focused fix.
